title: A Survey of Large Language Models in Psychotherapy: Current Landscape and Future Directions

bias_targets.methodology: Analyzing the distribution of languages used across 69 surveyed studies, quantifying the dominance of English-language corpora (70%) and highlighting the lack of multilingual resources.
Reviewing the literature to critique the direct translation of English mental health datasets, evaluating how such methods fail to reliably capture culture-specific psychological nuances.

Quantifying the focus of mental health conditions in current literature to demonstrate a severe imbalance, where common conditions like depression and anxiety are overrepresented while complex disorders like bipolar disorder are neglected.

Reviewing recent literature (e.g., Wang et al., 2024d) that systematically investigates unfairness in LLM predictive accuracy and outputs related to user demographic factors across multiple mental health datasets.
